chapter_title: Concerning the Four Great Days that have come forth from one another, together with the Four Nights
chapter_note: The chapter is predominantly systematic cosmological enumeration (four days/four nights; twelve hours/shadows) and reads largely as an older correspondential taxonomy. The main later intrusions are (a) hagiographic/compilational framing and beatitude-style closings (¶1, ¶6, ¶17), and (b) application that maps a cosmic register onto contemporary religious institutions (“church”, “sects”) inside otherwise cosmological sentences (¶5, ¶14–¶15), producing MIXED paragraphs.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic attribution (“Once again the enlightener speaks”) functions as compilation frame rather than cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: The first great day is the Father, the God of truth, the fir[st ... ... m]idst the aeons of his greatness, in his [l]iving kingdom. The twelve hours of this great day are the twelve great rich Gods of greatness. These, who are the first evocations that he evoked (to mirror) his greatness, he spread out to the four climes, three by three before his face.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, schematic cosmology: Father/aeons + a fixed twelvefold hour-structure mapped to divine beings and spatial ‘four climes’.

paragraphs.core_text: The second day is the Third Ambassador, the one who dwells in the light ship. His twelve hours are the twelve virgins that he evoked in his greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the same numbered-system mapping (day → cosmic being; hours → emanated twelvefold set) wholly within the cosmological system.

paragraphs.core_text: [The third day is the Pillar of Glory, the great porter that is greater than] all [the po]rters; the one that supports all [ ... ], those above and those below. Its twelve hours are the five sons of the First Man; the five sons of the Living Spirit, who support all the weights of the universe; together with the summons and the obedience, which are counted to their ten brethren. These are the twelve light hours of the third day.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Structural, taxonomic exposition: Pillar of Glory + paired pentads + two salvific ‘calls’ (summons/obedience) to complete a twelvefold set; no citation, no exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth day is Jesus the Splendour. His twelve hours are the twelve wisdoms, which are his [light] h[o]u[rs].
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed institutional locator phrase: “who [dwells in] his church” as a cosmos→community identification that likely reflects later application/institutional phrasing rather than the underlying day/hour cosmological taxonomy.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core is the day→being and hours→twelvefold ‘wisdoms’ mapping; the inserted ‘church’ anchor most naturally reads as later institutional application (even if ‘Jesus the Splendour’ itself is a cosmic entity).
Summary + beatitude (“Blessed is every one…”) reads as editorial closure/paraenetic tag rather than part of the systematic correspondential mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.26⟩ [ ... ]: For just as four day[s ex]ist, s[o] too four nights exist.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Programmatic connective that introduces the matching fourfold/night schema; functions inside the structural exposition rather than hagiographic frame.

paragraphs.core_text: The first night is the Land of Darkness. It has twelve black [shadows] therein, which are its dark h[o]ur[s]. The twelve shadows of the first night are the five elements of the Land of Darkness, [which] poured forth from its five sense organs; and [ ... ] which [ ... ] in its [fi]ve elements and its five [ ... ]; the five [sp]irits that dwell in its elements [ ... ]. These are the twelve shadows and spirits of the first night.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure cosmological correspondential schematization: night → realm; hours → shadows/spirits; twelve derived via pentads and ‘sense organs’—all internal to the system.

paragraphs.core_text: The second night is Matter, the sculptress [ ... ... ] who has sculpted [ ... ] and the entire ruling-power that is in the worl[ds of Darkness]. She has fashioned it in five sense organs, five [male] and five female, two per world; together with the fire and the lust [that] dwell in men and women, inflaming [them] inward to one another. These are the twelve spirits of this second night.
paragraphs.temporal_note: System-internal generative account: Matter as cosmic artificer; fivefold sensory structuring; male/female dualization; twelvefold totalization—no institutional address.

paragraphs.core_text: Indeed she, this Matter, the thought of death, ga[ve] the King of the realms of Darkness and his powers strength for the war and the fight, against the aeons of greatness. Yet, he was caught! They laid a snare for him through the Fi[rst M]an. [He] was ta[ken] t[o ... ] through the powers [ ... He] was brought up from the land of death and s[et ... ab]ove and below in the [whole] universe; in the five par[t]s in the heavens above, as well as the five [parts] in the earths below; together with the heat and the cold that are the father and the mother, their fire and their l[u]st.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic-mechanical cosmology (snare/rescue; above/below placements; pentadic divisions) presented as how the universe is structured—no later citation or church discipline.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the second night that is begotten from the first night. They laid a snare for her through the First M[a]n. She was brought up by the hand of the Living Spirit, and set in this composite univers[e ... ] he[r], above and below. The [upper side is the sense] organs of males; the lower side [ ... ] fe[mal]es.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Degree/descent language (“begotten from”) and cosmic engineering (upper/lower mapped to sexual ‘sense organs’) marks an older systematic layer.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.27⟩ The thir[d night is the five] worlds of flesh [ ... five] male, and five female; that were begotten from the powers [abo]ve. They have fallen upon the earth, being displayed in wh[at is d]ry and what is moist; together with the fire and the lust [that d]we[l]l in them, which drives them inward to one another.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic correspondential cosmology: worlds of flesh in pentads, rendered via elemental qualities (dry/moist) plus paired passions—still system-internal.

paragraphs.core_text: [Mat]te[r] herself, the thought of death, is the [mother] of them all; as among them she is named 'the night'. [The worlds] of male and female fleshes, together with the fire and the l[ust], shall [ ... ] twelve hours of [ ... ... ] night. Again, [it] too, the third night that is in the worlds of fl[e]sh, was begotten from the second night; which the Living [Spir]it crucified in the uni[verse ... , ab]ove and below in heaven [ ... ... ].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Internal derivation logic (‘begotten from’), and cosmic salvific mechanics (‘crucified in the universe’) without NT citation formulae—fits the teaching substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth night is the law of Sin, which is the dark spirit who speaks in the twelve spirits. They are the nakedne[ss]es, the twelve zodiacal signs of Matter. They are her thrones; she who is made public, as she sculpts and is displayed in the Old Man.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed institutional identification: “the twelve sects” (cosmos→contemporary religious grouping application).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying core is a zodiacal/twelvefold cosmology (Sin-spirit → twelve spirits → zodiacal signs). The ‘sects’ gloss applies the scheme outward to the editor’s religious landscape.

paragraphs.core_text: And, also, the hours of this fourth night that is the Old Man, are the twelve e[vi]l spirits; the [ ... ] of the Old Man, which [are ... ... ... ... di]fferentiate the day and night [ ... ... of] death.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed application clause: “who reigns in the sects” as an institutional/worldly anchor appended to the cosmological ‘Old Man’ schema.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core is a continuation of the twelvefold ‘hours’ taxonomy within the ‘Old Man’ complex; the ‘sects’ phrase is an outward-pointing editorial application.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the fourth night [ ... ] that have come forth of one another. One has [ ... ... ] just like the days of lig[ht ... ] they manifested one another. So als[o ... ] they did arise out of one another.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Structural recapitulation of the fourfold emanation sequence (‘come forth from one another’), consistent with the chapter’s schematic teaching voice.
Beatitude/paraenesis (“Blessed is he…”) functions as an editorial closing tag rather than a component of the cosmological mapping itself.
